clue.text: Writer's loose garter is seized by angry mob

indicators.note: something seized by a mob is held in its grip, so the scrambled letters sit inside the mob's letters

parts.note: an angry mob is a mad rabble

indicators.note: a loose garter has come undone, signalling that its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novelist's garter slips off while an enraged crowd grabs hold of her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' turns GARTER into RGARET, which 'is seized by' puts inside MAD RABBLE after its first two letters. The 's of 'Writer's' stands for 'is', so the definition is just the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Drabble is an English novelist, author of The Millstone and The Radiant Way.

clue.text: One judging when flowers come up around the 5th of August?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the reversed flowers go around the picked letter, holding it inside
in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: roses are flowers

indicators.note: count to the fifth letter of the following word and take it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who will judge the garden show when the flowers bloom in early August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' reads the flowers bottom to top in this down clue, and 'the 5th of' picks a single letter of August for 'around' to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor is a person who evaluates or judges, for instance tax liability or an insurance claim.

clue.text: Put out by something that gets up your nose?

definitions.meaning: to put out a candle is to extinguish it

definitions.text: something that gets up your nose?
definitions.meaning: powdered tobacco sniffed up the nostrils; the phrase also means something irritating

explanation.definitionFit: To snuff a candle is to put it out, and snuff is powdered tobacco inhaled through the nose.

clue.text: Relative going to northern Switzerland to relax

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A family member travels to the north of Switzerland for a holiday to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclench a fist or jaw is to loosen it, so to let go of tension.

clue.text: Shrine left in beauteous valley

indicators.note: the letter for left sits within the valley's name

parts.note: the Vale of Tempe in Thessaly, Greece, was celebrated by poets for its beauty

explanation.surface: A holy shrine is found abandoned in a lovely valley.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMPE is a classical byword for a beautiful valley, so 'beauteous valley' points at the name rather than a description.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a building for worship, and a shrine is a sacred place of devotion.

clue.text: Retired churl wept buckets

annotationWithheld.why: Retired churl wept buckets (9): BLUBBERED is LUBBER (churl) in BED, and 'Retired' gives both BED and the containment (in bed), one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Minor excursion finds worthy soul on winning streak

parts.note: a saint is a worthy soul, abbreviated ST
to be on a roll is to have a run of successes

explanation.surface: A good-hearted person on a lucky run goes for a short trip.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the saint comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely short walk, a modest outing on foot.

clue.text: Stimulant — speed — given to terrorists on road enveloped by gas

indicators.note: the gas wraps around the other pieces, so they sit inside its letters

parts.note: methane is a gas
MPH, miles per hour, measures speed
ETA was the Basque separatist group
the M1 motorway, written MI, is the stock crossword road

explanation.surface: A drug called speed is handed to terrorists on a road shrouded in gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like the drug's slang name and part of the definition, but it is miles per hour; 'enveloped by' wraps the gas round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Methamphetamine is a powerful synthetic stimulant drug of the amphetamine family.

clue.text: Oaf formerly adopting an Owenesque poetic device

parts.note: an ass is a foolish oaf

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the word for formerly takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: once means formerly, at one time

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool from the past takes up a poetic technique Owen liked.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilfred Owen, the First World War poet, is noted for half-rhymes built on vowel echoes; 'adopting' takes the article into the word for formerly.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance is the repetition of vowel sounds in nearby words, a device Wilfred Owen used heavily.

clue.text: Tipsy ambassador's anything but stiff

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A slightly drunk diplomat has become loose and relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and flexible, the opposite of rigid.

clue.text: Grope and pull around, coming back very happy

indicators.note: returning means the combined letters are read backwards
the word for pull goes around the word for grope

parts.note: to lug is to pull or drag
to grope is to feel one's way

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles and tugs about, then returns in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the pull round the grope, and 'coming back' turns the whole combination, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleeful means full of glee, delighted.

clue.text: Music playing, initially, con brio in pub

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit within the pub's abbreviation

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a new order
take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A performance played with spirit in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con brio' is a musical direction meaning with vigour, which disguises 'initially' taking just C; 'playing' scrambles that with the rest to give IBROC for 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is a piece of classical bagpipe music, theme and variations, from the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Silence in music, or in Hamlet's last words?

definitions.meaning: a pause in a score, marked with its own symbol

explanation.definitionFit: A rest is a notated silence in music, and the word appears in Hamlet's dying line.

clue.text: An inverted fish swallowed live before the war

indicators.note: the reversed fish takes the next word inside it
the fish's name is turned back to front

parts.note: a mullet is a fish
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: An upside-down fish gobbles something alive in the days before the conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' turns the fish into TELLUM, and 'swallowed' takes the word for live into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antebellum is Latin for before the war, used especially of the American South before the Civil War.

clue.text: Joke with Muse, taking note of impeccable behaviour

parts.note: a pun is a play on words, a joke

indicators.note: the Muse takes the note in, holding it inside her name

parts.note: Clio is the Muse of history
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A wordplay gag paired with an inspiring Muse who writes down notes about good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: Clio is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth; 'taking' has her name take the note inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctilio is a fine point of etiquette, or exactness in observing correct conduct.

clue.text: Smear the President's hat

parts.note: to tar someone is to smear their reputation
Bush was the US President when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: Someone besmirches the headgear of the US President.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarbush is a tasselled brimless felt cap like a fez, worn in the Middle East.

clue.text: Flaw in drunk's report of rapture about printer's measure

indicators.note: the slurred word goes around the measure, holding it inside

parts.note: rapture is bliss, and a drunk slurring it would say blish
an em is a printer's unit of width

explanation.surface: A slurring drunk's description of ecstasy contains a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs bliss into a lisping version; 'about' wraps that round the typographic unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a mark or defect, a flaw spoiling something's perfection.

clue.text: Played both sets with maximum effort

indicators.note: the letters are played around with, arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A tennis player gave everything in both sets of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; give it your best shot means try as hard as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Your best shot is the greatest effort you can make, as in 'give it your best shot'.

clue.text: Nice mess getting press coverage as peace initiative

indicators.note: the press word covers the rearranged letters, wrapping them inside

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the town's letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A messy situation in Nice gets press coverage as a peace proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' scrambles the French city into ENIC, and 'coverage' has the press word wrap it.
explanation.definitionFit: An irenicon is a proposal designed to promote peace, especially between churches.

clue.text: Resort receiving account of gambler's haunt

indicators.note: the resort word receives the account abbreviation into itself

parts.note: recourse is a resort, something turned to for help

explanation.surface: A holiday resort hears an account of where gamblers go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot but means a last resort; 'receiving' takes the abbreviation in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is where horses race and punters place bets, a classic gambler's hangout.

clue.text: Compelling melon to be produced in court

indicators.note: the melon is brought into court, placed inside its abbreviation

parts.note: Ogen is a variety of melon

explanation.surface: A melon is to be presented in court as convincing evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Ogen is a small sweet melon variety first bred in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is compelling, persuasive and convincing.

clue.text: Biblical dupe keeping bridge players up with sense of foreboding

indicators.note: the reversed name keeps the bridge players inside it
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Esau was tricked out of his birthright by Jacob
North and East are partners' seats at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A gullible Bible figure keeps the card players awake, full of anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns only the dupe's name, giving UASE, and 'keeping' holds the two bridge seats inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease is a feeling of anxiety or disquiet, a sense that something is wrong.

clue.text: Trial held during Mao Tse Tung's revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things around, so the found letters are read backwards
the letters are held within the run of the name

explanation.surface: A test is staged during the Chinese Revolution under Mao.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held during' finds TSET across 'Tse Tung', and 'revolution' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is a trial or examination of something's quality.

clue.text: US city where there's no more curry?

indicators.note: these words signal that the following word is removed from the city

parts.note: Baltimore is a city in Maryland

explanation.surface: In which American city have they run out of curry?
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a wok-like metal bowl.

clue.text: Man or monkey, say, mostly holding a doctor's instrument

indicators.note: the trimmed word holds the next pieces inside it
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a man or monkey is an example of a two-legged animal
a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A man or ape is mostly clutching a doctor's tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the two-legged creature, and 'holding' takes the article and doctor inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The bagpipe is a wind instrument with drones and a chanter fed from a bag.

clue.text: Sports venue where Dumas gets it wrong

indicators.note: getting it wrong suggests the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: The French novelist Dumas makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium is a large arena for sports events with tiered seating.

clue.text: The one foreign soldier with a turban

parts.note: in French, l'un means the one
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A single foreign soldier wears a turban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a cloth worn as a loincloth or wrapped as a turban in South Asia.

clue.text: Deity enters tonsured cow

indicators.note: the god enters the shaved word, sitting inside it

parts.note: tonsured means with the head shaved, shorn
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A god walks into a cow with a monk's haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk's head; 'enters' puts the Norse god inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A shorthorn is a breed of cattle with short curved horns.
